text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM stengthens ties with its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines. (p1)
- Chemicals concern DSM on target for 13 pct full-year net profit growth. (p1)
- Bourses and stockbrokers use indices to lure clients. (p1)
- Philips Electronics is to join Japan's concern Sony and Sharp in flat screen TV project. (p4)
- Housing market expanded by more than 33,000 new units in the first half of 1997. (p5)
- KLM fleet uses some 2.5 bn tonnes of kerosene in 1996/97 fiscal year from 2.3 tonnes a year earlier. (p2)
- Investors react negatively to DSM's higher profit. (p2)
- Mobile phone company Libertel's subscribers to get discount in Free Record Shops. (p2)
- Amsterdam Hotel Krasnapolsky sees first half 1997 net rise sharply to Dfl 3.7 (2) million. (p29)
- Belgian/Dutch bank insurer Fortis to pay Dfl 665 to extend its stake in ASLK from 49.9 to 60 pct. (p29)
- Investment fund Optimix remains optimistic about prospect for the stockmarket. (p31)
- Publisher VNU's participation in Flemish commercial TV VTM books Dfl 19.2 pct losses in 1996. (p6) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Insurer Aegon is to force investors in FGH to sell the remaining 0.25 pct of their shares. (p1)
